When I had first read about compression and saw Red's charts with triangles and the like I got myself mixed up in looking for a pattern and putting triangles all over the screen. This did not help me.

I believe you have the concept in your mind and you know the answer just something is getting twisted.

Why would we want compression? so price is able to make large moves once it hits our zone of choice. If we are looking to sell at supply we would hope that the demand zones are consumed beneath so it can fall for good r:r. Vice versa for buying.

It is optimal to trade from fresh zones because once a zone has been tested it is more likely to fail. This is why compression to supply looks like price is spiking down as it moves upwards. It is testing all of the levels below and makes it highly likely that once price reaches supply it will fall straight through these zones because they are consumed.

May i suggest to start with higher TF(as boring as it sounds...) M1 can be an information overload.

From a different angle: When an army advances from a base it will go full speed(pole/Rally/Drop) until it hits a well defended area(previous strategic Base). Depending on the defense the army has a few choices: - Camp in front of the enemy and create a new Base/Range, waiting who will blink first. (RB?, DB?) - A tactical retreat to SR, triggering part of the defense, then push and crush the Base. - Push straight away and risk exhaustion, creating small bases near a major enemy base => CP. The enemy could feign weakness => LQ-spike, hit hard and retake the small bases with massive force.

Box and label everything(on chart, paper or mental) HTF => LTF:)
